Common OSINT Mistakes

One of the most common mistakes is starting an investigation without defining the question. This creates large amounts of irrelevant information and makes it difficult to determine when the research is complete.

Another common mistake is treating search ranking as evidence of reliability. Search engines help researchers discover information, but ranking does not establish that a source is original or accurate.
Researchers can also mistake repetition for corroboration. Several websites repeating the same claim may all originate from one unverified source.

OSINT can contain incomplete, outdated, duplicated, manipulated, biased, or decontextualized information. Search engines have coverage gaps, online content can disappear, identities can be difficult to verify, and AI can create false connections. Strong conclusions therefore require corroboration and transparent limitations.
